Plot whether each candidate of a grid converged, lies on a boundary and replicated its best log likelihood

Source: R/wildcards.R
plot_trust.Rd

plot_trust() plots whether the estimate of each candidate of an enumeration grid can be relied on: did it converge, is it on a boundary, and did more than one start reach its best log likelihood.

Usage

plot_trust(x, main = NULL, subtitle = NULL)

Arguments

x

An enumeration grid from enumerate_lpa(), enumerate_lca(), enumerate_classes() or enumerate_regressions(). A grid of group-class families (enumerate_classes(family = )) has no such view and is refused.

main, subtitle

Title and subtitle of the plot. NULL (default) keeps the view's own text.

Value

A ggplot object.

Errors:

  • latents_nothing_to_plot when the package returned x but this function has no plot of it: a fitted model, a comparison or another result, or a grid of group-class families. For an object of the wrong kind, the message names the plot functions that apply to it;

  • latents_not_a_fit when x is not a fit, grid or other result of the package, for example a data frame;

  • latents_missing_package when ggplot2 is not installed.

Details

The x-axis is the number of classes and the y-axis the number of group classes, so each tile is one candidate. A grid with several covariance structures has one panel per structure. The fill and the text of a tile give the status of the candidate:

  • replicated: converged, and two or more starts reached the best log likelihood;

  • once: converged, but only one start reached the best log likelihood, so a higher maximum may exist;

  • n/a: converged, with no replication count stored;

  • boundary: converged with an estimate on the boundary of the parameter space;

  • not conv.: the best start did not converge;

  • not fitted: the candidate has no log likelihood.

Under the status the tile gives the number of starts that reached the best log likelihood, for example 2x. Replication does not prove that the global maximum was found.

See also

get_replication() for the counts of starts as a table; get_candidates() for converged and boundary; plot_selection().

Examples

grid <- enumerate_lpa(faithful, c("eruptions", "waiting"),
                      n_profiles = 1:3, model = "EEI",
                      n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
plot_trust(grid)
